case_title: Surinder Singh v. State (Union Territory of Chandigarh)
aggravating_circumstances: Use of a service pistol, inebriated condition, pointing gun at victim
mitigating_circumstances: No motive or planning, clean record, passage of time, no injury caused
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.307 and Arms Act s.27, sentenced to 3 years rigorous imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused, a police officer, entered the residential office of the victim in an inebriated condition. After consuming water, he pulled out his service pistol and aimed it at the victim, directing the victim's clerk and steno to leave the room. The accused moved around the table, pulled the lever of the pistol, and prepared to fire. The victim lunged at the accused, causing the bullet to hit the ceiling. The accused attempted to fire again but failed, and a bullet fell from the pistol. The incident was reported to the police, and the accused was arrested. Forensic evidence confirmed that the cartridge recovered from the victim's office was fired from the accused's service pistol. The accused claimed an alternate version of events, but the trial court found it dubious. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts, medical reports, and forensic evidence to establish the accused's actions.
